answer: Stake-weighted identity resists sybil attacks: every agent locks a deposit to register in the registry, an orchard of bonded accounts, and its voting, grading, and payment weight scales with the locked amount, not with how many identities it runs. A sybil attacker minting many copies still commands one pool of capital, so each copy gets a tiny weight and the swarm gains nothing; the attacker's cost is the opportunity cost and slashing risk of every idle deposit. A finished task pays a pearl only when the claimant's locked ember exceeds the task's value, so throwaway identities cannot collect.
